event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: AMD’s 2023 Form-10-K frames COVID-19 as a still-evolving, multi-faceted threat that is already disrupting operations while also posing sizeable forward-looking risks.  The company cites concrete, current impacts—supply-chain interruptions, workforce productivity losses, logistics delays—as well as broader macro-economic, capital-market and consumer-demand uncertainty.  Language such as “we have experienced” shows the risk is not merely hypothetical, yet most disclosures remain qualitative and unquantified.  Mitigating actions (long-term purchase commitments, remote-work adjustments, liquidity facilities) slightly temper severity but do not eliminate exposure.  Because the filing date (Feb-2023) sits less than three years after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time Decay Principle allows relatively high scores; nonetheless, the absence of dollar figures or hard metrics keeps individual sentences below a maximum-impact “10.”  Overall, AMD presents a live, material, but largely un-quantified pandemic risk landscape.

evidence_list.snippet: • The ongoing novel coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links COVID-19 to material adverse effects on business and finances.
Uses strong severity language ('materially adversely affect').
Generic, forward-looking with no specifics or quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear acknowledgement of material risk but stated in generic terms without detail, yielding a mid-high score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing novel coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic has caused government authorities to implement numerous public health measures, including at various times vaccination and testing requirements and recordkeeping, quarantines, business closures, travel bans, and restrictions related to social gathering and mobility, to contain the virus.

components.reason: Details specific widespread measures disrupting normal commerce.
Connects measures directly to the pandemic’s evolution (recent, ongoing).
Descriptive rather than company-specific impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence outlines broad disruptive context but lacks AMD-specific impact; risk relevance moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: Various state and federal rules are issued and updated on an ongoing basis, at times in conflict and/or with minimal notice.

components.reason: Highlights regulatory volatility increasing operational uncertainty.
No direct consequence or severity quantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides uncertainty signal but minimal direct impact detail, so lower score.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced and expect to continue to experience disruptions to our business as these changing measures have, and will continue to have, an effect on our business operations and practices.

components.reason: Confirms AMD has already suffered disruptions—direct present impact.
Projects continuing future impact (‘expect to continue’).
No dollar amount or scale provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct admission of ongoing operational disruption drives higher risk score despite lack of quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: While our employees gradually return to office, we continue to monitor our operations and public health measures implemented by governmental authorities in response to COVID-19.

components.reason: Indicates incomplete workforce normalization and need for monitoring.
Implies some mitigation through monitoring and phased return.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows lingering operational adjustments but also mitigation, giving a low net risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: It is uncertain as to when all health measures put in place to attempt to contain the spread of COVID-19 will be lifted.

components.reason: Highlights continued uncertainty over regulatory environment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pure uncertainty without direct AMD linkage merits small risk points.

evidence_list.snippet: If there are further waves of the virus, health measures may be reimplemented and we may need to further limit operations or modify our business practices in a manner that may impact our business.

components.reason: Identifies concrete operational restrictions if pandemic worsens.
Conditional, forward-looking statement.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential for renewed disruption elevates risk but remains conditional.

evidence_list.snippet: If our employees are not able to perform their job duties due to self-isolation, quarantine, lockdown measures, unavailability of COVID 19 tests, travel restrictions or illness, a reluctance or refusal to vaccinate, or are unable to perform them as efficiently at home for an extended period of time, we may not be able to meet our product schedules, roadmaps and customer commitments and we may experience an overall lower productivity of our workforce.

components.reason: Details direct labor-force constraints leading to missed schedules and lower productivity.
Covers multiple specific causes (quarantine, testing, vaccination issues).
No quantified magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational consequences on product schedules drive higher mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: Even when COVID-19 health measures are lifted or modified, our employees’ ability or willingness to return to work may delay the return of our full workforce and the resumption of normal business operations.

components.reason: Points to lingering workforce availability issues even post-restrictions.
Still hypothetical; no metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes plausible delay risk but with limited severity detail.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 continues to impact the global supply chain causing disruptions to service providers, logistics and the flow and availability of supplies and products.

components.reason: Highlights ongoing global supply-chain disruptions affecting inputs and logistics.
Describes present tense impact (‘continues to impact’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Active, non-hypothetical supply-chain disruption yields a strong risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced some disruptions to parts of our supply chain as a result of COVID-19 and we adjust our supply chain requirements based on changing customer needs and demands.

components.reason: Confirms AMD has already faced supply-chain disruptions.
Mentions adaptive measures (adjust requirements).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct impact (+) offset by described mitigation, so moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: We have taken efforts to maintain a stable supply of materials to meet our production requirements through long-term purchase commitments and prepayment arrangements with some of our suppliers.

components.reason: Describes concrete mitigation actions (long-term commitments, prepayments).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Purely mitigating sentence, decreasing overall risk perception.

evidence_list.snippet: If we are unable to procure a stable supply of equipment, materials or substrates at a reasonable cost, it could have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Links supply shortages directly to material adverse business effects.
Conditional forward risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential but serious supply risk keeps mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: We may also assess our product schedules and roadmaps to make any adjustments that may be necessary to support remote working requirements and address the geographic and market demand shifts caused by COVID-19.

components.reason: Indicates need to redesign schedules/roadmaps due to pandemic shifts.
Contains internal mitigation stance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Minor operational adjustment with mitigation; low net score.

evidence_list.snippet: If the supply of our products to customers is delayed, reduced or canceled due to disruptions encountered by our third-party manufacturers, back-end manufacturers, warehouses, partners, suppliers or vendors as a result of facility closures, border and port restrictions or closures, transportation delays, lockdown measures, labor shortages or workforce mobility limitations, it could have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple concrete disruption channels leading to material adverse effect.
Forward-looking, contingent risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive supply-chain risk scenario drives strong but conditional score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 has in the short-term and may in the long-term adversely impact the global economy, creating uncertainty and potentially leading to an economic downturn.

components.reason: Acknowledges both immediate and prolonged macro-economic impact.
Indirect rather than company-specific.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Macro framing relevant but less directly tied to AMD operations.

evidence_list.snippet: This could negatively impact consumer confidence and spending causing our customers to postpone or cancel purchases, or delay paying or default on payment of outstanding amounts due to us, which may have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Connects economic downturn to concrete revenue and credit risks.
Potential, not yet realized.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies clear revenue-cycle risks, earning a mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Even in times of strong demand for our products, the worldwide economic environment remains uncertain due to COVID-19 and such demand may not be sustainable over the longer term.

components.reason: Warns current demand could evaporate due to pandemic uncertainty.
No specificity or quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Gives high-level demand risk, moderate weighting.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 has also led to a disruption and volatility in the global capital and financial markets.

components.reason: Notes capital-market volatility, impacting financing ability.
Generic macro statement.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Macro-level observation, limited direct AMD effect; modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: While we believe our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments along with our Revolving Credit Agreement and cash flows from operations will be sufficient to fund operations, including capital expenditures, and purchase commitments, over the next 12 months and beyond, to the extent we may require additional funding to finance our operations and capital expenditures and such funding may not be available to us as a result of contracting capital and financial markets resulting from COVID-19, it may have an adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Admits possible funding constraints due to pandemic-driven market contraction.
Highlights liquidity mitigation (cash, revolver) reducing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Liquidity risk noted but heavily mitigated, producing low score.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which COVID-19 impacts our business and financial results will depend on future developments, which are unpredictable and highly uncertain, including the continued spread, duration and severity of the outbreak, the appearances of new variants of COVID-19, the breadth and duration of business disruptions related to COVID-19, the availability and distribution of effective treatments and vaccines, and public health measures and actions taken throughout the world to contain COVID-19.

components.reason: Acknowledges high uncertainty and multiple future risk drivers.
Lacks company-specific data.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad uncertainty acknowledgment; moderate but not detailed.

evidence_list.snippet: The prolonged effect of COVID-19 could materially adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Echoes potential for material adverse impact if pandemic persists.
Generic statement; no evidence of magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: General caution without specifics yields modest score.
